Editor’s note on gedes and the withdrawn emendation Godes (Wi 23).

entry.dictScrap: g[æ]d Convent, Kirchenstift; gn: gedes [nicht Godes zu ändern!] Wi 23
entry.note: Liebermann keeps the manuscript’s gedes (“of the convent”) at Wihtred 23, against the emendation Godes (“God’s”) made by earlier editors and by Liebermann himself in vol. I, where his German translation still reads “einen Slavenknecht [eines] Gottes[hauses]”. In his commentary on the clause (Gesetze III) he withdraws the emendation, as he had already done in this entry (vol. II, p. 85) and at vol. II, p. 757: gæd is attested in Old English poetry for societas, “fellowship”, and the clause means “accuses a convent’s bond-servant in their [the monks’] chapter”. See Wi 23, with his commentary and the modern translations, which also follow the manuscript (Attenborough “a bond servant of a company”, Whitelock “of a community”).
